answer: Stake-bond sybil resistance: each agent locks collateral C; joining k identities costs k·C. A slashing condition triggers on equivocation or failed proofs, burning the full bond. The horizon for a farm is negative EV once slashing probability p exceeds reward/C. The prism of per-identity returns then splits honest from sybil: linear rewards, k-fold capital. Nectar (yield) only flows to identities surviving audit; a 10-identity farm at p=0.15 loses ~1.5 bonds per epoch, exceeding rewards. Bonds make scaling linearly costly while slashing makes cheating strictly unprofitable.
